subject: Intermittent 5xx responses from Chronos5B — fallbacks activated / post-incident briefing
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@acme.ai>, support@acme.ai
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 5xx responses from Chronos5B — fallbacks activated

Hi Emily / Acme team,

Quick update from Redwood: we detected an elevated rate of 5xx and timeout responses from model Chronos5B between ~08:47–09:05 PT this morning for a subset of long-context requests. We activated short-term fallbacks to limit customer impact:

- Traffic routing: requests to Chronos5B that exceed 8k tokens are being routed to chronos-lite for the next 60 minutes.
- Model variant fallback: chronos5b-safe (quantized variant with tighter memory controls) is enabled for traffic with full-context preservation requirements.
- Autoscaling: we increased pool capacity for the Chronos family in us-west to reduce queuing.

Attachments: chronos-traffic-spike-snapshot.csv (sample traffic and 5xx timestamps).

What we know so far (preliminary): a kernel-level regression combined with a KV-cache eviction pattern caused memory pressure on a narrow set of requests (long sequences + large prompt embeddings), which led to OOMs and subsequent timeouts (5xx). Engineering is actively triaging; we prioritised fallbacks to keep your runtime stable.

Can you confirm whether you saw increased latency or failed requests on your end in the 08:45–09:15 window? Any specific request IDs or example prompts would help. We'll share a formal post-incident note after the internal RCA.

Apologies for the disruption — I know this impacts real traffic. If you'd like an immediate call, I can join right away.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0174

From: Emily Zhao <emily@acme.ai>

Cc: support@acme.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx responses from Chronos5B — fallbacks activated

Thanks Vivek — we did see a spike in errors and some downstream timeouts around 08:50–09:00 PT. Several user-facing calls retried and returned inconsistent outputs after retries (some returned partial tokens then 5xx).

Example request ID: 9f3a-2b7c (we have logs if you need them). Latency increased from ~120ms to ~2.6s for a percentage of calls; error rate went from ~0.2% to ~4.7% in our telemetry.

Two immediate asks:
1) If the fallback to chronos-lite changes output semantics, we need a short compatibility note so our frontend can detect and handle it gracefully.
2) Please confirm whether any customer data was exposed during the incident (we need this for our internal compliance).

Appreciate the quick response.

—Emily
Emily Zhao
Head of Platform Integrations | Acme.ai
emily@acme.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@acme.ai>, support@acme.ai
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 13:30:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx responses from Chronos5B — fallbacks activated / preliminary findings

Emily — thanks for the quick data. We pulled the request IDs you supplied and added them to the triage. Preliminary update and immediate next steps: 

Prelim root cause (under investigation):
- A kernel optimization deployed last night introduced a non-deterministic memory accounting regression for large KV-cache entries.
- Under high long-sequence concurrency (your workload + internal autoscaling bursts) the regression allowed transient oversubscription of GPU memory, causing OOMs and cascading 5xx responses.
- The fallbacks we enabled (chronos-lite and chronos5b-safe) avoid the kernel path and reduce memory pressure, but do have small differences in logits under edge-case prompts.

Mitigation / timeline: 
- Immediate: rollback of the kernel patch (completed 12:25 PT) — we observed error rates drop to baseline for the majority of traffic.
- Canary: a targeted patch to the kernel accounting logic is scheduled to roll to 2% of traffic at 15:00 PT today; if stable we'll expand to 100% in controlled increments.
- Configuration: we increased KV-cache retention thresholds and temporarily capped per-request context length to 10k tokens for Chronos family (expected impact: <0.5% of your requests based on your telemetry).
- Postmortem: draft attached (postmortem-draft-chronos5b.pdf). The draft includes timeline, technical root cause, and permanent fixes (kernel accounting correction, memory telemetry improvements, stronger pre-deploy load tests).

Regarding your asks:
1) Compatibility note: we'll publish a short compatibility guide in the next 45 minutes summarizing behavioral differences between chronos-lite / chronos5b-safe and Chronos5B (mainline). We'll include a small fingerprint test you can run to detect variant responses client-side.
2) Data exposure: no evidence of customer data leakage — errors were internal to the serving path (OOMs/timeouts) and did not alter access controls. We will include the full verification steps in the postmortem.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call this afternoon to walk through the details and the patch plan.

Thanks for your patience,
Vivek
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Chronos5B — internal follow-up (customer comm + credits)

Monica / Ben — internal notes for the thread with Acme:

- Customer-impact summary: Acme saw ~4.7% error spike; key window 08:47–09:05 PT. They reported increased latency and inconsistent outputs after retries; provided request IDs.
- Engineering actions taken: rollback completed (12:25 PT), KV-cache thresholds increased, token-cap applied, chronos-lite fallback active until canary finishes.
- Next steps: expand canary at 15:00 PT if no regressions, then paper-roll to 25/50/100. Postmortem draft is attached and marked for review by SRE and Product.
- Customer offer: recommend offering Acme a one-month service credit for the incident and a follow-up joint RCA session (30–45 min). Need your approval to issue the credit and to book the session for next Tue/Wed.

Please advise on credit amount (suggest 30% of October host usage for Acme) or alternate. Also confirm whether Legal needs to review the postmortem attachment before we share the final version.

Thanks,
Vivek
